items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: We had one incident of each. Piano, violin, tenor saxophone, trumpet, trombone, and drums. And the drummer was Victor Burton who wrote the Sob and Blues.

ctx.x: Well, it may not have been his fault, you know. It may have been some pressure put on him by the publishers or something of the book.

No, he... No, the book didn't... This... Durrell Black. Wasn't it Durrell Black? No, it was with Al Rose. I know. They sent me a testimonial, and I'm a jazzy model, and my daughter has his frame. I guess they sent out a million of them, because Dr. Block says, I'm waiting until you see you come out. You never came out. I said, I don't leave the house at night, Dr. Block. I said, I have a sick wife, because you know you're treating her, you know. Well, this... My daughter's so proud of it, she had it framed in it.…
I know him from his records with Nichols and the Wolverines.
